title: Guidance on Tax Exemption Applications Ensures Disability Rights Are Not Missed
summary: To safeguard the rights of persons with disabilities, New Taipei City Tax Bureau recently sent exclusive guidance notices for applying for exemption from vehicle license tax to two specific categories. Eligible individuals should apply early; after approval, they can enjoy limited tax exemptions from the application date. The bureau stated that the targets mainly include: first category, persons with disabilities without a driver's license or vehicle, their spouse or relatives within second degree of kinship sharing the same household, or vehicles owned by such relatives with registration address matching the person's household; second category, persons with disabilities who have a driver's license but no vehicle, their spouse or relatives within second degree of kinship sharing the same household who own a vehicle. The notice includes application case number and exclusive QR code.
body:

Eligible individuals should apply early; after approval, they can enjoy limited tax exemptions from the application date. title: Social care is for us all, and we all must fund it | Letters
summary:
Readers respond to Polly Toynbee’s article on the new prime minister’s commitment to a fair system
Polly Toynbee (Battles loom over social care, but this fight must be won. At last, we have a PM who believes that, 29 July) is right that reforming England’s broken social care system will require winning the “attention, hearts and minds” of a public that knows little about it. Yet one of the biggest barriers to reform is that social care itself remains widely misunderstood, and public debate often reinforces narrow assumptions about who uses it.
Social care is too often equated with care homes and dementia services for older people. While these are vital, they are one part of a wider system. Demand has grown fastest among working-age disabled adults who are largely missing from the public and political narrative. As such, the assertion by Polly Toynbee that “the old must pay for the old” is incorrect. Social care is relied on by people of all ages.
 Continue reading...

title: Old House Extension Subsidy Application Deadline September 11; Tainan City Strengthens Promotion and On-site Guidance
summary: The Tainan City Government continues to promote the Ministry of Interior's Old House Extension Functional Renewal Plan, accepting applications until September 11, 2026. Briefing sessions have been held and on-site advisory teams started July 15 to provide application consultations. The subsidy applies to apartments aged 30+ years, 4-6 floors, and low-rise legal detached houses, requiring a structural safety assessment first. It can cover up to 65% of project costs, including facade repairs, roof waterproofing, pipeline updates, accessibility facilities, and age-friendly equipment, aiming to extend building lifespan and improve safety and quality. As of August 4, 11 briefing sessions have been conducted.
body:
The Tainan City Government continues to promote the Ministry of Interior's Old House Extension Functional Renewal Plan, accepting applications until September 11, 2026. Briefing sessions have been held and on-site advisory teams started July 15 to provide application consultations. The subsidy applies to apartments aged 30+ years, 4-6 floors, and low-rise legal detached houses, requiring a structural safety assessment first. It can cover up to 65% of project costs, including facade repairs, roof waterproofing, pipeline updates, accessibility facilities, and age-friendly equipment, aiming to extend building lifespan and improve safety and quality. As of August 4, 11 briefing sessions have been conducted.

title: Disability Only Can Live in Institution? Long‑Term Care Expert Reveals Discharge Transition and Home Rehabilitation Assessment
summary: An 85‑year‑old woman suffered a duodenal ulcer with upper GI bleeding, leading to prolonged bed rest, severe weakness and loss of independent living. Her family struggled with the choice between home care and institutional placement, especially due to the lack of barrier‑free facilities at home and gaps in caregiving. A director from Taichung City’s Renai Comprehensive Long‑term Care Institution stresses that returning to a familiar environment is the elder’s wish, but successful discharge depends on the elder’s health, family support, and home care conditions. Multidisciplinary care and rehabilitation training are highlighted as key to rebuilding daily living abilities.

title: Bamboo scaffolding blocks tactile paving in To Kwa Wan, endangering visually impaired persons
summary: In To Kwa Wan, multiple bamboo scaffolding structures have been erected on tactile paving, causing visually impaired individuals to collide with them. The Buildings Department states this violates guidelines and demands contractors to correct the issue. Industry workers note such violations are common. Visually impaired resident Lung哥 says the location is extremely dangerous for the visually impaired, causing head injuries and continuous bleeding when bumped. He has lived in To Kwa Wan for over 30 years and daily goes out to buy groceries or see a doctor, but as the old district ages, more construction work increases hazards, such as the scaffolding at No. 71 Ma Tau Wai Road blocking the tactile paving. Lung哥 explains that visually impaired people rely on traffic lights with auditory signals to cross roads; white canes sweep the ground, not overhead, so they assume there are no obstacles above and end up hitting them.

In To Kwa Wan, multiple bamboo scaffolding structures have been erected on tactile paving, causing visually impaired individuals to collide with them. The Buildings Department states this violates guidelines and demands contractors to correct the issue. Industry workers note such violations are common. Visually impaired resident Lung哥 says the location is extremely dangerous for the visually impaired, causing head injuries and continuous bleeding when bumped. He has lived in To Kwa Wan for over 30 years and daily goes out to buy groceries or see a doctor, but as the old district ages, more construction work increases hazards, such as the scaffolding at No. 71 Ma Tau Wai Road blocking the tactile paving. New Taipei councilor Liu Mei-fang questions the Cultural Bureau about the Hsiang Theatre Group, which includes disabled performers and 'slow fly angels', after winning the 8th New Taipei Cultural Award but now facing dissolution, six months of unpaid wages, inability to pay labor and health insurance, and a credit crisis due to a canceled US tour that caused nearly NT$5 million in losses. She urges the bureau to swiftly create an emergency assistance project for cultural groups, with early warning and support mechanisms to aid struggling small-to-medium teams.

title: Woman Files Sexual Harassment Complaint After Being Groped While Buying Potstickers; Wheelchair-Bound Man with Cognitive Impairment Not Prosecuted
summary: In New Taipei City, a man surnamed Wu was accused by a woman identified as A of groping her buttocks while she was buying potstickers at a shop in Xinzheng Changping Street in March. Wu admitted he was the person captured on surveillance but denied the act, claiming he could not remember. His defense lawyer argued that Wu suffers from cognitive and consciousness impairments, supported by medical documentation from his wife. Consequently, prosecutors determined that Wu's action of touching A's buttocks could not be confirmed as having the intentional mens rea for sexual harassment, resulting in a decision not to prosecute.
body:
In New Taipei City, a man surnamed Wu was accused by a woman identified as A of groping her buttocks while she was buying potstickers at a shop in Xinzheng Changping Street in March. Wu admitted he was the person captured on surveillance but denied the act, claiming he could not remember. His defense lawyer argued that Wu suffers from cognitive and consciousness impairments, supported by medical documentation from his wife. Consequently, prosecutors determined that Wu's action of touching A's buttocks could not be confirmed as having the intentional mens rea for sexual harassment, resulting in a decision not to prosecute.

title: The care system fails to care for parents | Letters
summary:
Anna Bird reflects on Matilda Davis’s story and says families need support early – before exhaustion becomes a crisis
Matilda Davis’s story should force us to confront an uncomfortable truth and something that parent carers tell us every day: for too many families raising disabled children, the care system fails to care (Matilda in pieces: what one mother’s suicide reveals about the carers broken by the system, 11 August).
Parent carers need timely access to support in the home, short breaks and services that recognise and respond to their own needs as well as those of their disabled child. Most importantly, families need support early – before exhaustion becomes a crisis.
 Continue reading...

title: When You Realize Not Everyone Can Just Go: Understanding Mobility Inequality from the CRPD Perspective

summary: The Tainan City government secured roughly NT$250 million to renovate all 585 public toilets citywide, including those at Kunshen Seawater Bathing Area, Jiangjun Mashaogou, and Xiaoying Sugar Railway Park. Improvements feature better ventilation and lighting, water‑saving fixtures, and comprehensive barrier‑free, family‑friendly and gender‑inclusive spaces with thoughtful details. The Environmental Protection Bureau also upgraded hardware and stepped up daily management and maintenance, completing 25,244 on‑site toilet inspections from January to July. Inspections follow toilet‑grade schedules and conduct unannounced spot checks on cleanliness, facility integrity, and ventilation odors. So far 4,802 toilets have earned the top excellence grade and 32 the excellent grade, showing strong overall performance. To further raise cleaning and management standards, the EPB has recently held toilet‑cleaning training at the Degao Li Activity Center and the Jiaji District Office…
body:
The Tainan City government secured roughly NT$250 million to renovate all 585 public toilets citywide, including those at Kunshen Seawater Bathing Area, Jiangjun Mashaogou, and Xiaoying Sugar Railway Park. Improvements feature better ventilation and lighting, water‑saving fixtures, and comprehensive barrier‑free, family‑friendly and gender‑inclusive spaces with thoughtful details. The Environmental Protection Bureau also upgraded hardware and stepped up daily management and maintenance, completing 25,244 on‑site toilet inspections from January to July. Inspections follow toilet‑grade schedules and conduct unannounced spot checks on cleanliness, facility integrity, and ventilation odors. So far 4,802 toilets have earned the top excellence grade and 32 the excellent grade, showing strong overall performance. title: Southern Railway underground project nearing completion; Minister Chen Shih-kai inspects and urges finishing 1-2 months ahead of schedule
summary: A comprehensive report from the Living Center states that the Taiwan South Railway underground project, which has been under construction for over six years and eagerly awaited by Tainan residents, has entered the final stage. Minister of Transportation Chen Shih-kai visited for inspection, checking the latest train information display system, platform escalators, and station air-conditioning equipment one by one. Currently, including accessibility inspections and fire safety checks, all have passed. A pre-operational review is scheduled for September before opening. Chen also urged that, aiming to finish the original year-end target, efforts should be made to open one or two months earlier.
body:
A comprehensive report from the Living Center states that the Taiwan South Railway underground project, which has been under construction for over six years and eagerly awaited by Tainan residents, has entered the final stage. Minister of Transportation Chen Shih-kai visited for inspection, checking the latest train information display system, platform escalators, and station air-conditioning equipment one by one. Currently, including accessibility inspections and fire safety checks, all have passed. A pre-operational review is scheduled for September before opening. Chen also urged that, aiming to finish the original year-end target, efforts should be made to open one or two months earlier.

title: Taipei City bus service performance indicators evaluation results released
summary: Taipei City announced the results of the first half of 2026 urban bus operation service performance evaluation, with five operators receiving excellent ratings: Southeast Bus, Dasan Bus, Capital Bus, Metropolitan Bus, and Taipei Bus. The Taipei City Transportation Bureau's Public Transport Division said on the 21st that urban buses carry over one million passengers per day on average, with satisfaction rates above 95% over the past three years, making them an important public transport tool. The Taipei City Bus Office pointed out that to continuously improve bus service quality, this evaluation is based on five major categories: station facilities and services, vehicle equipment and safety, passenger service quality and driver management, corporate operations and management, as well as accessible station facilities, services, vehicle equipment and safety, totaling 27 indicators for comprehensive assessment, using objective indicators to fully examine each bus operator's operations and service...
body:
Taipei City announced the results of the first half of 2026 urban bus operation service performance evaluation, with five operators receiving excellent ratings: Southeast Bus, Dasan Bus, Capital Bus, Metropolitan Bus, and Taipei Bus. The Taipei City Transportation Bureau's Public Transport Division said on the 21st that urban buses carry over one million passengers per day on average, with satisfaction rates above 95% over the past three years, making them an important public transport tool. The Taipei City Bus Office pointed out that to continuously improve bus service quality, this evaluation is based on five major categories: station facilities and services, vehicle equipment and safety, passenger service quality and driver management, corporate operations and management, as well as accessible station facilities, services, vehicle equipment and safety, totaling 27 indicators for comprehensive assessment, using objective indicators to fully examine each bus operator's operations and service...

title: Taipei Ciyuan Garden tour bus crashes into crowd, injuring two; vehicle hits accessibility facilities before stopping
summary: In Taipei City's Xinyi District, Ciyuan Garden experienced a shocking traffic accident on the afternoon of the 22nd. A 70-year-old man surnamed Yang driving a tour vehicle on an uphill slope inside the garden suddenly lost control, striking a parked shuttle bus and then hitting a 25-year-old pedestrian surnamed Ruan beside the road. After impact, the tour vehicle did not stop but continued forward, eventually slamming into the garden's accessibility facilities before coming to a halt. The crash injured both Yang and Ruan, though both sustained only minor injuries and were hospitalized without serious complications.

title: Tainan Social Affairs Bureau Activates Care Mechanism for Vulnerable Groups Amid Heavy Rain
summary: Due to continuous heavy rainfall causing flooding, Tainan City's Social Affairs Bureau launched disaster response operations and set up six shelters accommodating 40 people. Deputy Bureau Chief Ye Zhi-ming visited shelters in Yan-shui, An-nan, and An-ping to comfort victims. The bureau's physical love bank resources were mobilized to distribute daily necessities. Mayor Huang Wei-che said all 12 district social welfare centers have been activated, with 127 social workers proactively checking on elders, persons with disabilities, homeless, and special-needs families, confirming disaster impact and needs, and providing material assistance, welfare resource links, and follow-up support.
body:
Due to continuous heavy rainfall causing flooding, Tainan City's Social Affairs Bureau launched disaster response operations and set up six shelters accommodating 40 people. Deputy Bureau Chief Ye Zhi-ming visited shelters in Yan-shui, An-nan, and An-ping to comfort victims. The bureau's physical love bank resources were mobilized to distribute daily necessities. Mayor Huang Wei-che said all 12 district social welfare centers have been activated, with 127 social workers proactively checking on elders, persons with disabilities, homeless, and special-needs families, confirming disaster impact and needs, and providing material assistance, welfare resource links, and follow-up support.

title: Sheltered Workshops Hit Hard! Lin Guo-zhang Leads Yilan Team to Buy 300 Mooncake Boxes; Wen-chang Chen Criticizes Wu Zong-xian as Unqualified for County Mayor
summary: The Kuomintang caucus in the Legislative Yuan forcibly cut the Presidential Office's confidential expenses, causing Mid-Autumn gift box orders for sheltered workshops across Taiwan to face a funding shortage. Yilan County mayoral candidate Lin Guo-zhang led the Yilan team in a press conference titled 'Yilan People Take Care of Yilan People, Using Action to Support Social Welfare Organizations,' emphasizing that political struggles should not harm the innocent, and that the budget freeze affects disabled workers' right to survive and work. He announced a joint purchase of 300 mooncake boxes with the DPP to support the workshops. Legislator Wen-chang Chen strongly criticized Wu Zong-xian, saying he lacks the qualifications to run for county mayor.
body:
The Kuomintang caucus in the Legislative Yuan forcibly cut the Presidential Office's confidential expenses, causing Mid-Autumn gift box orders for sheltered workshops across Taiwan to face a funding shortage. Yilan County mayoral candidate Lin Guo-zhang led the Yilan team in a press conference titled 'Yilan People Take Care of Yilan People, Using Action to Support Social Welfare Organizations,' emphasizing that political struggles should not harm the innocent, and that the budget freeze affects disabled workers' right to survive and work. He announced a joint purchase of 300 mooncake boxes with the DPP to support the workshops. Legislator Wen-chang Chen strongly criticized Wu Zong-xian, saying he lacks the qualifications to run for county mayor.

title: Chairman Zhang Jun holds forum with disabled persons: Government must truly listen to disabled needs, make it a basic standard for Hualien governance
summary: Chairman Zhang Jun held a forum with disabled persons and families; disability organization reps and parents of persons with intellectual disabilities gave suggestions on disability employment, barrier-free transport, public spaces, and social participation. Zhang Jun said these are not individual family difficulties but basic rights the county must address, and he pledged to turn the suggestions into budgetable, trackable, and verifiable policies, making disability rights a basic standard for Hualien governance. Disability group reps noted that job hunting is hard for disabled persons in Hualien, and the county lacks large accessible buses that can accommodate multiple people and wheelchairs; when organizing outings, they often need to borrow vehicles from other counties, incurring high costs and limiting disabled persons' opportunities to leave home and engage society. They urge the county to evaluate purchasing and establishing reasonable usage.
body:
Chairman Zhang Jun held a forum with disabled persons and families; disability organization reps and parents of persons with intellectual disabilities gave suggestions on disability employment, barrier-free transport, public spaces, and social participation. Zhang Jun said these are not individual family difficulties but basic rights the county must address, and he pledged to turn the suggestions into budgetable, trackable, and verifiable policies, making disability rights a basic standard for Hualien governance. Disability group reps noted that job hunting is hard for disabled persons in Hualien, and the county lacks large accessible buses that can accommodate multiple people and wheelchairs; when organizing outings, they often need to borrow vehicles from other counties, incurring high costs and limiting disabled persons' opportunities to leave home and engage society. They urge the county to evaluate purchasing and establishing reasonable usage.

title: Mayor Lu Hsiu-yang's 'Cancel Order' Remark Draws Green Camp Dissatisfaction, Criticized by Cheng Kung-jin as 'Political Queen Cancelling Order Show'
summary: Taichung City Council member Cheng Kung-jin pointed out that the Presidential Office had originally planned to purchase Mid-Autumn Festival products from 37 nationwide sheltered workshops and disability organizations, but due to the freezing of the 2026 annual special expenses fund, the orders could not be fulfilled, affecting five disadvantaged groups in Taichung and thousands of boxes. Cheng criticized Mayor Lu for downplaying the cause of the budget freeze and only shouting 'central government cancelled the order, Taichung bears it,' ignoring the mention of the freeze, turning disadvantaged groups into sacrificial props of a political show. He called Lu the 'cancel order queen,' prompting a rebuttal from KMT councillor Huang Hsin-hui asking whether there was a special instruction not to buy Mid-Autumn gifts from sheltered workshops, and noting that the Presidential Office must reallocate funds while Lu herself has had billions cut in the council.
body:
Taichung City Council member Cheng Kung-jin pointed out that the Presidential Office had originally planned to purchase Mid-Autumn Festival products from 37 nationwide sheltered workshops and disability organizations, but due to the freezing of the 2026 annual special expenses fund, the orders could not be fulfilled, affecting five disadvantaged groups in Taichung and thousands of boxes. Cheng criticized Mayor Lu for downplaying the cause of the budget freeze and only shouting 'central government cancelled the order, Taichung bears it,' ignoring the mention of the freeze, turning disadvantaged groups into sacrificial props of a political show. He called Lu the 'cancel order queen,' prompting a rebuttal from KMT councillor Huang Hsin-hui asking whether there was a special instruction not to buy Mid-Autumn gifts from sheltered workshops, and noting that the Presidential Office must reallocate funds while Lu herself has had billions cut in the council.
